impact.why: First measurement of leniency and rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline; the screen-threshold-as-focal-point finding is directly actionable for enforcement design.

execution.why: Pre-registration with timestamps, positive and placebo controls, run ledger and permutation tests are convincing; 4-pool cells, post-hoc pool extension and narrow screen coverage limit it.

presentation.why: Clear structure, tables and Figure 1 carry the story; a few internal number clashes, two Haiku value sets and a half-empty page 5 cost polish.

summary_three_sentences: The report replays the Bigoni et al. (2012) cartel and leniency experiment with LLM sellers from four models, scoring them against the published human values under a pre-registered rule. It shows that told-only fines, leniency and rewards remove explicit cartels far more than in humans, yet three of four models keep supracompetitive prices silently, and a price screen lowers those prices but turns its threshold into a focal price. Proven within this lab game: the controls behave, explicit cartels vanish under enforcement while silent pricing stays well above Nash, and the screen effect holds in the three arms tested; human comparisons are untested point contrasts.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, Abstract, last two sentences (screen sentence and 'three of seven' sentence)
top_fixes.change: Scope the screen claim to the arms actually run and disclose the 4-pool and permutation caveat in the headline, so the abstract cannot be read as favourable selection.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: In the three arms where it ran, a pre-registered price screen lowers prices without a penalty (Sonnet without a channel 7.36 to 4.00, exactly the threshold). Haiku reproduces three of seven results (two on the first four pools; Result 3 bootstrap only).

top_fixes.where: Page 4 Finding 1 (formation 'equals the human one'), page 7 Discussion ('prices settle just below it'), page 2 Introduction (Fish et al. 'when they can talk'), LLM Usage Statement (claude-opus-5-5)
top_fixes.change: Remove the four internal contradictions: label the 0.716 formation as first 4 pools, say Sonnet prices at the threshold, drop 'when they can talk' for Fish, and state Opus was not a tested subject or delete it.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: On the first four pool sessions Haiku's formation rate matches the human 0.716; with all eight it is higher (Figure 1). ... a known threshold becomes a focal point, and Sonnet prices exactly at it.

top_fixes.where: Page 5, empty lower half after the scorecard paragraph; page 4, start of Section 4 Results
top_fixes.change: Pull Figure 1 up onto page 5 to close the gap, and use the freed space for one sentence giving the outcome of each pre-registered hypothesis H1 to H4, which Methods announces but Results never resolves.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Pre-registered hypotheses: H1 (cartels without an authority) supported for all four models; H2 ... ; H3 ... ; H4 ... . Decision rules as registered; extensions are marked as such.

contradictions.where: Page 4, Finding 1 vs Figure 1 panel 1 and Table 3 Result 1
contradictions.what: Text says Haiku formation equals human 0.716; 8-pool figure and Table 3 (0.630 + about 0.15) put Haiku LF formation near 0.78.

contradictions.where: Abstract and Finding 3 vs Discussion 'What this means for a competition authority'
contradictions.what: Abstract and Finding 3: Sonnet prices exactly at the threshold 4; Discussion: prices settle just below it.

contradictions.where: LLM Usage Statement vs Abstract and Methods
contradictions.what: Usage statement lists claude-opus-5-5 among models under test; abstract and Methods name only four models without Opus.

contradictions.where: Introduction vs Related Work on Fish et al. (2024)
contradictions.what: Introduction says agents collude 'when they can talk' citing Fish; Related Work says Fish showed collusion autonomously, without communication.

contradictions.where: Validity paragraph (placebo) vs Table 2 and paraphrase sentence
contradictions.what: Placebo minus fine +0.275 from 0.714 implies fine incidence 0.439 (4 pools, App. A); Table 2 and paraphrase sentence use 0.401 (8 pools); sample unstated.

contradictions.where: Methods (one-sided permutation) vs Table 4 and Finding 2 p 0.029
contradictions.what: With 4 vs 4 pools the minimum one-sided exact p is 1/70 = 0.014; complete separation reported as 0.029 suggests two-sided or a different count.

overclaims.why: 'These' are prices under fine, leniency, reward for three models; the screen ran only on no-channel arms and Haiku fine.

overclaims.sentence: a false-positive rate of at most 1.1 percent
overclaims.why: Measured only against four scripted legitimate strategies in this game, not competitive LLM agents or real demand shocks.

overclaims.sentence: A price screen reaches that silence
overclaims.why: Qwen and Llama were never screened, Sonnet only without a channel; prices fall to the threshold, not to Nash.
Result 3 fails the permutation test (p 0.099) and the 4-pool scorecard.

overclaims.sentence: told-only leniency and reward remove the most explicit cartels
overclaims.why: Holds for Haiku only; Sonnet and Qwen reach zero already under the fine, Llama is flat across regimes.

overclaims.sentence: the report rule acts in the humans' direction with a far larger effect
overclaims.why: Human values are untested point estimates; report-rate gap 0.543 vs human about 0.415 is not 'far larger'.

overclaims.sentence: The whole programme is cheap and complete
overclaims.why: 'Complete' is unsupported: screen, paraphrase and placebo arms cover only some models and regimes.

red_lines.note: Mild: the abstract headline 'three of seven' uses the 8-pool scorecard, added by amendment after the 4-pool result (two of seven) was known; the body discloses this and the permutation miss, the abstract does not. Design and human values are correctly credited to Bigoni et al.; LLM use is disclosed.
